page: Microsoft Azure M1ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an arm64-based architecture. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance provides a dedicated single vCPU paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:16 CPU-to-memory ratio designed for memory-intensive workloads that require modest compute capabilities.

Hardware specifications highlight an ARM processor without integrated GPUs or local instance storage. Storage relies exclusively on remote attached volumes, with native support for Premium Storage tiers. Compute allocation remains fully dedicated, preventing noisy neighbor contention on the single core, although it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX vector extensions.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the ARM-based profile provides a dense allocation of memory per core, avoiding the higher resource costs typically tied to multi-core deployments when only RAM footprint is required. Tradeoffs include reliance on network-attached block storage and limited single-threaded processing capacity, making it unsuitable for highly parallelized or compute-bound pipelines.

The M1ps_v4 instance is targeted at workloads prioritizing large memory footprints over heavy processing, such as small-to-medium in-memory caches, lightweight database engines, proxy caching layers, and ARM-compatible background data buffering services.
description: Microsoft Azure M1ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a dedicated 1-vCPU configuration built on an arm64 processor architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 1:16 compute-to-memory ratio intended for low-concurrency applications that demand substantial memory buffers. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, utilizing remote block storage with Premium Storage capabilities instead, and operates without hardware GPU accelerators. With its dedicated core execution model and ARM power profile, the M1ps_v4 offers an economical infrastructure option for hosting memory-heavy software components without paying for surplus compute cores. It is suited for lightweight database tasks, distributed memory caching nodes, and basic message queuing services adapted for ARM environments.
